note: The decisions AWK-37's seed executes, separated from the script that applies
them. Read by seed_period_and_forms.py, asserted by period-and-forms.test.ts.
Everything here is a DECISION, not a derivation. Which composer matches which
IMSLP page by an exact folded name, which era that page carries, and which of
the 351 played works IMSLP holds a page for are all computed live by
imslp_harvest.py and land in imslp-harvest.json -- deliberately, because a
second copy of a derivable fact is a second thing to drift. What lives here is
what the wiki cannot answer: the names it files differently, the composers it
does not hold, the era to pick when it names two, and every form judgement.
THE INVARIANT THIS EXISTS TO PROTECT is that a correction survives a
re-harvest. ADR-0007 keeps IMSLP out of the build for three reasons and the
third is that 'corrections made by hand must survive'. The applier layers this
file over the harvest, so re-running imslp_harvest.py -- which overwrites its
own output entirely -- cannot clobber a judgement recorded here.
WORKS ARE KEYED BY ENTRY ID, NOT BY TITLE, and the value is the title as a
checked redundancy. (composer, title) is NOT unique: `The Nutcracker Suite`
appears twice under Tchaikovsky, and the two rows are exactly the case this
ticket exists to distinguish -- one is Ellington's and must read Jazz. The
applier re-reads each title from the space and aborts on a mismatch, so a
renamed or deleted work fails loudly instead of writing to the wrong row.
SINCE AWK-65 NOT EVERY ROW IS A SETTLED DECISION. `workForms` also holds blank
rows -- the works no automatic route can answer for, seeded so that curating one
is filling an array rather than authoring an object. A blank is a decision not
yet taken, and `settled` marks one taken as "it stays empty". Nothing else in
this file is pending.
Archive `sortName` -> IMSLP page name, for every composer an exact folded
match does not settle. A null means CHECKED AND ABSENT, not unchecked --
the same three-state distinction ADR-0006 draws on `concert.attended`, and
for the same reason: a considered finding must not read as an unreviewed
row. Every null below was confirmed against the full 55,461-page index.
The absences are what ADR-0007 predicted -- living composers and the
American 20th century -- plus the premieres the archive holds and no
library does. Each one takes a hand period in `composerPeriods` below.
The 19 arranger-only records AWK-23 created are NOT here and must not be
added. They hold zero works, so they are never in scope, and leaving their
period null is correct rather than a coverage failure.
`Bach, Johann Sebastian (arr. by Stokowski)` WAS a different case and was
here until AWK-79. It was original xlsx import data -- bso-graph.json holds
it -- not one of AWK-23's records, and it held one work, so it came into
scope under AWK-66 when a sixth LIYO concert reached the Toccata and Fugue.
The harvest confirmed zero candidates, which was expected: the parenthetical
is a filing name no library uses.
THE RECORD'S SHAPE WAS WRONG AND AWK-66 DID NOT FIX IT. ADR-0005 puts the
arranger on `work.arranger`, and the work already carried it correctly
(`Orchestration`, arranger 6CIojL7Jfv7xmRjMRAsaF6) -- so the credit was
recorded twice, once properly and once inside a composer's name. AWK-79
merged the record into `cmp-bach-johann-sebastian` on 2026-09-01, by hand
in the web app, and its row here went with it: the clean Bach matches IMSLP
and needs no alias. Left as prose so the next person reads the history
rather than wondering why AWK-66's paragraphs above count a record that is
not there.
Hand-assigned `composer.period`, for the two cases the harvest cannot close.
These OVERRIDE the harvest wherever both speak, so a correction made here
survives a re-run.
FIRST: the composers IMSLP does not hold, every one of them null above.
ADR-0007 called these trivial -- 'a 2019 premiere is Modern without
research' -- and for the premieres and the living composers that holds.
Three are not trivial and are dated deliberately: Marie Cowan (d. 1919) set
Waltzing Matilda in 1903, Richard Addinsell wrote the Warsaw Concerto in
1941, and Randall Thompson's Alleluia is 1940. All three are Early 20th
century and none of them is Modern.
SECOND: the five composers IMSLP files under TWO eras. `composer.period` is
a single Symbol, so the wiki cannot be taken verbatim here and something has
to choose. The rule applied is the era of the repertoire THIS ARCHIVE holds,
not the span of the composer's life, because the field exists to browse
these 351 played works and nothing else:
Schubert     Romantic, and the archive's only Schubert -- Symphony No. 5,
1816 -- takes a Classical override in `workPeriods`. This is
ADR-0007's own worked example, the Beethoven First-vs-Ninth
case, arriving on a different composer.
Sibelius     Romantic. Symphonies 2 and 5 and the Violin Concerto,
1902-1915, are late Romantic rather than modernist.
R. Strauss   Romantic. Six works from 1883 to 1948; the tone poems and
Rosenkavalier carry the weight.
Hindemith    Early 20th century. One work, Nobilissima Visione, 1938.
Shostakovich Early 20th century. Four of the six are 1925-1945; only the
Tenth and the Cello Concerto sit past 1950.
The last five are judgement calls on a browse filter, not facts. They are
the rows to argue with first.
THIRD, added by AWK-66 and REMOVED by AWK-79: `Bach, Johann Sebastian (arr.
by Stokowski)`, which came into scope with a sixth LIYO concert. It read
`Baroque`, because the composer axis answers for the COMPOSER and the one
work the record held is Bach's Toccata and Fugue. The orchestration is
Stokowski's and it is Early 20th century, which is a fact about the
arrangement -- ADR-0005 puts that on `work.arranger`, where it already was,
and ADR-0007's Ellington case shows the work override carrying an
arrangement whose IDIOM changed. An orchestration does not change the idiom,
so no override was declared. AWK-79 then merged the record into
`cmp-bach-johann-sebastian`, which IMSLP files under one era, so the row is
gone and the period decision above stands as the reason the work took no
override rather than as a row.
FOURTH, added by AWK-82: `Diamond, David`, who came into scope with the
three LISFA festival Concerts and is the FIRST case since AWK-37 where the
harvest holds no page at all for a composer the space needs a period for --
period-and-forms.test.ts is what caught it, by asserting that no in-scope
composer is left unresolved.
`Modern`, and the reasoning is the cohort rather than the dates alone. The
American composers in this archive split across the boundary: Copland,
Gershwin, Ives, Piston and Leroy Anderson are Early 20th century, while
Barber, Bernstein and John Adams are Modern. Diamond (1915-2005) is
bracketed exactly by Barber (1910) and Bernstein (1918), and the one work
the archive holds -- Rounds for String Orchestra, 1944 -- is contemporary
with the Barber and Bernstein it would sit beside on a browse page. Filing
him with Copland instead would be defensible on his birth year; it would
put him a shelf away from his own generation.
Like the five two-era rows above, this is a judgement call on a browse
filter rather than a fact, and it belongs in the same list of rows to argue
with first.
`work.period`, which overrides the composer's. Keyed by entry id, valued by
title -- see the header on why (composer, title) will not do.
ADR-0007 argues this field is worth having on the strength of two cases and
both are here. Ellington's Nutcracker is the record's own example: the work
inherits Tchaikovsky's Romantic and is Jazz, and since AWK-23 the row is
identifiable by `arranger` rather than by a name string, which is why the
id below is the one carrying cmp-ellington. Schubert's Fifth is the
transitional case, a Classical symphony by a composer filed as Romantic.
DELIBERATELY SHORT. The harvest reads `X style` off matched work pages and
the applier writes an override only where that style DISAGREES with the
composer's period -- an agreeing style is not an override, it is the
inheritance already working, and writing it would put 300 redundant values
in the space for nothing. So this list holds only what the wiki cannot say.

note: The mechanical half of job 2: each retired `genre` entry's NAME mapped to
the forms every work carrying it receives. ADR-0007 keeps the seventeen
names as the starting vocabulary, so all seventeen appear, and sixteen map
to themselves.
`Aria` is the one that does not, and it is the bucket ADR-0007 dismantles.
It holds 13 works of which about four are arias; the rest were captured by a
regex matching `,\s*from\b`, which is any excerpt. So the name does NOT
carry over automatically -- `workForms.arias` names the genuine ones and
everything else in the bucket is left to the derived Excerpt rule and its
own row. Mapping Aria to Aria would migrate the error rather than the data.
`Excerpt` is DERIVED, not curated, and this is the one place a regex over
titles survives this ticket.
ADR-0007 calls the Aria bucket an 'accidental discovery': the pattern that
built it was matching excerpts correctly and only filing them wrongly. 'Is
this drawn from a larger staged work' is a real fact the title states in
plain sight, so it is read rather than judged -- which is exactly why a tag
set can hold it when a single field could not.
Applied ON TOP of every other rule, never instead of one: `Selections from
Romeo and Juliet Suites` is Suite, Ballet AND Excerpt.
The hand-curated half of job 2: work id -> the forms that work receives, on
top of whatever genreForms and the derived Excerpt rule already produced.
Nothing is ever removed, because the multi-valued field IS the repair -- the
Firebird Suite becomes [Suite, Ballet] rather than having to choose, which is
the choice the old single field got wrong.
KEYED BY WORK, NOT BY FORM. This was five form-named buckets until the
curation backlog made the shape wrong: a bucket per form means a work wanting
two forms is listed twice, and every new form value needs a new bucket.
`Ballet Suite from "La Strada"` was already listed twice, in `ballets` and
`filmMusic`, which is the shape failing on 28 entries rather than 104.
The 28 below are the MIGRATION REPAIRS -- works whose retired genre was wrong
or incomplete, not works that had none. Three groups, and they are the three
failures ADR-0007 diagnoses:
* 16 BALLETS filed as suites, because their titles say Suite and Suite was
tested first. They kept Suite and gained Ballet -- and since AWK-80 the
row names BOTH, because the Suite half used to arrive through `genre`
and AWK-66 deleted that field (see the AWK-80 paragraph below).
`Selections from Romeo and Juliet Suites` sat in the Aria bucket instead
-- the `, from` pattern reached it first -- so it gains both, plus
Excerpt from the derived rule. The three works already filed as Ballet
are correct and absent here.
* The 13-strong ARIA bucket, taken apart. Six are genuine (three of them
duets, kept because Aria is the vocabulary's only word for a sung operatic
number); four are dances named as such by their own titles; one is film
music; one needs Excerpt the derived rule cannot see. Mapping Aria to Aria
would have migrated the error rather than the data.
* `Scenes from I Pagliacci` writes `from` with no comma before it and no
quoted title after, so the Excerpt pattern misses it. Naming the one case
is cheaper than loosening a regex to bare `\bfrom\b`, which would catch
every title merely containing the word.
AWK-66 ADDED FOUR MORE, and they are the first rows here for works OUT OF
SCOPE. Widening the genre -> forms mapping past the played works carried 199
of the 203 out-of-scope Works holding a `genre` with no judgement at all.
These four are the entire residue, all of them from the `Aria` bucket that
genreForms maps to nothing on purpose:
* Two are named `Excerpt from ...`, which the derived rule cannot see --
no comma before `from` and no quoted title after, the same gap
`Scenes from I Pagliacci` fell through.
* `Papageno's Aria (Sc. 9) from The Magic Flute` is a genuine aria AND an
excerpt, and falls through the same gap, so it names both.
* `Tales from the Vienna Woods Waltzes` is a waltz misfiled as an aria --
a clean specimen of the ~6% ADR-0007 measured as actively WRONG rather
than merely thin.
An out-of-scope row cannot be checked against the harvest, because the
harvest only covers the played works. The title redundancy still holds: the
applier re-reads every title from the space and aborts on a mismatch, which
is the check that actually protects a renamed or deleted row.
AWK-80 (2026-09-06) ADDED SIX ROWS AND WIDENED FOURTEEN, and the cause is
one event: AWK-66 deleted `work.genre` on 2026-09-01, so the genreForms term
of the applier's union is empty forever after. Every row written as `keeps
X and gains Y` had only ever declared Y, and 19 in-scope works began
reporting a permanent CONFLICT -- the space held the form genre used to
supply and nothing here computed it. A row now names the WHOLE set a work
should hold, minus what the harvest and the derived Excerpt rule still
supply. The 14 ballet rows gain Suite; Riverdance, La Gioconda's Dance of
the Hours, Aida's Triumphal March, the Liebestod and the Warsaw Concerto are
new rows for the same reason.
The sixth is the one AWK-80 was opened for. `7FdM6FH19h52lHS8EnFx1B` --
Tzigane, a Contentful-generated id because the Work was entered by hand for
the 1992-07-17 LIYO concert -- is `[Rhapsody]` and NOT `[Concerto, Rhapsody]`.
IMSLP carried Rhapsody for it from 2026-08-30 until the wiki withdrew the
category on 2026-08-31; Concerto was its hand-set genre. Alex settled it on
2026-09-06: Ravel's own subtitle is `rapsodie de concert`, a concert
rhapsody, not a concerto. The web app was edited to `[Rhapsody]` first,
because the applier only ever adds, and this row is what keeps the
decision from being the next re-harvest's casualty.
THE ROWS HERE ARE NOT THE WHOLE STORY, and that is recorded rather than
fixed. Measured 2026-09-06, 337 Works (172 in scope) hold forms that no
harvest row, no row here and no Excerpt match produces -- Symphony,
Concerto, Overture, mostly -- all of them genre's former output. They never
conflict because an empty computed set skips the check, so the applier
leaves them alone; but a `forms` field cleared in the web app has no
re-derivation path. Whether those ~340 belong here, in a frozen snapshot,
or nowhere is an open decision on AWK-80, not a gap in this file.
THE WORKS CARRYING NO FORM AT ALL ARE NOW HERE, AS BLANK ROWS, and that is
AWK-65 reversing a decision this note used to argue for. They lived in
docs/archive/form-curation.md and nowhere else -- a worksheet nothing reads --
on the reasoning that omission already said "considered, left blank", so an
empty `forms` array said nothing a reader could trust. What that shape cost was
that curating one meant authoring the whole object: id, title, forms, copied by
hand out of a markdown table. The 114 blank rows below exist so that filling one
in is typing a form name into an array that is already there, under an id and a
title already checked against the harvest.
WHAT OMISSION USED TO CARRY, `settled` NOW CARRIES. A blank row is ambiguous in
a way an absent row was not: it reads as both "not looked at yet" and "looked
at, and it stays empty". ADR-0007 expects the second for a real share of these
-- The Planets is a Suite or nothing -- so a row decided to stay empty takes
`"settled": true` beside its empty array. A blank row without it is untouched
backlog. That is the three-state device `composerAliases` spends a null on, and
it is here for the same reason: a considered finding must not read as an
unreviewed row.
EVERY BLANK ROW IS ALSO A TITLE CHECK NOW, which is a real change in what the
pass aborts on. plan_works builds `titles_expected` from every row here, so all
114 titles are compared against the live space and a work renamed in the web app
stops the whole run -- the period half included -- where before it was ignored.
That is the loud failure this file's header paragraph asks for, but it is new
surface, and it is the one cost of this shape worth knowing before a rename.
`workFormsFilled` in `guards` counts the rows carrying at least one form;
`workFormsRows` counts them all. Curating a batch moves the first, and only a
scope change moves the second. The applier is unaffected either way: a blank row
plans no write, because the union of the harvest, the row and the derived
Excerpt rule is empty for it, so curating ten at a time still costs nothing and
a re-run still reports nothing to do.
A form must be one of the 34 in archive-schema.json. That list is a Contentful
`in` validation and migrate_schema.py is additive -- it will NOT reshape a
field that already exists -- so a new value is a schema edit in the web app,
not an edit here.
AWK-65 TOOK IT FROM 25 TO 34 (2026-09-07), and the nine are Essay, Fugue, Hymn,
Intermezzo, Pavane, Poem, Polka, Romance and Tango. They are not a widening for
its own sake: each one is a word a specific work needs and the 25 could not
supply -- Faure's Pavane, the Delius intermezzo, Piazzolla's Tangazo and
Mackey's Redline Tango, the three hymns, Cowell's fuguing tune and Kempton's
ricercar, Barber's Essay, Griffes' Poem, the Lark Ascending's Romance, and the
Perpetuum Mobile polka. ADR-0007 permits this in as many words -- it "fixes the
mechanism, not the enumeration" -- and its own eight additions were made the
same way, for the same reason, one curation round earlier.
THE NINE ARE DECLARED HERE AND NOT YET IN THE SPACE, which is a drift this
repo cannot detect. archive-schema.json says 34 and the live `in` validation
still says 25 until someone edits it in the web app by hand; the tests pass
either way, because nothing here reads the live list. A row using one of the
nine therefore fails at PUBLISH, entry by entry, rather than in the suite. The
guard against that is a test -- see period-and-forms.test.ts -- that fails if
any row uses one of the nine, and it is meant to be deleted the day the web-app
edit lands, not before.

note: IMSLP work-page category -> archive form. ADR-0007 requires a whitelist
because the wiki's category namespace is flat and mixed with operational
junk -- `OM Parts`, `Sibley Mirroring Project`, `Scordatura`, `Quintuple
time` all sit alongside `Symphonies` on the same page.
MEASURED YIELD IS SEVEN WORKS. Of the 124 carrying no genre, 25 match an
IMSLP page at all and 7 of those carry a whitelisted category: An American
in Paris, Boléro, Capriccio Espagnol, Concert pour petit orchestre, España,
Night on Bald Mountain and Parade. The whitelist is kept wider than that
yield on purpose, so a later work added to the archive is covered without
editing it.
The reason the yield is so small is structural rather than fixable. The
archive names excerpts (`Act II, Carmen`) where IMSLP names works, and the
modern repertoire has no IMSLP pages AT ALL -- Barber, Bernstein, Britten,
Khachaturian, Glass, Tippett, Rota, Piazzolla and John Williams each return
zero work pages, being in copyright. Which is to say the harvest cannot
reach precisely the works that need it most.
`Boleros` maps to Dance rather than to a Bolero form: ADR-0007 cites IMSLP
filing Boléro under both `Boleros` and `Dances` as evidence FOR a tag set,
and the archive's vocabulary has no Bolero. `Incidental music` maps to
Excerpt for the same reason the derived rule exists -- it says the piece
was written for a larger staged work.
Abort thresholds, not comments -- the same device merge-composers.json uses,
and `--force` downgrades them to warnings the same way.
THE COUNTS ARE LIVE-DERIVED AND WILL MOVE. AWK-37 was written against 322
works and 147 composers; AWK-59's LIYO transcription had moved the archive
to 338 and 153 before this ran, and ADR-0007's own 104 uncategorised works
are 114. So these are recorded as the numbers this pass was PREPARED
against, and a drift means re-read the diff rather than push through it.
AWK-64 moved them again, to 346 and 156, and this is the third re-baseline
in three tickets -- which is the paragraph above being right about itself.
The three Tilles Center LIYO Concerts brought 8 works and 3 composers into
scope: the 6 Works that transcription created, plus 2 that already existed
and had been out of scope because no attended Concert reached them. The 3
composers are Walter Piston and Ferdinand David, both new, and Cesar
Franck, who was already in the space. Franck is the interesting one -- he
gains a period AND the accented spelling, because IMSLP files him as
`Franck, César` and the fold is exact.
THE GUARD WORKED AS DESIGNED, and this note records that it was re-read
rather than forced. `--force` was available and would have been the wrong
move: it silences the abort without correcting the file, leaving the
declaration permanently claiming a scope the space no longer has.
`maxComposerWrites` and `maxWorkWrites` are ceilings on a single run. They
exist because the applier writes to published entries: a bug that widened
scope would otherwise rewrite the whole archive before anyone read the log.
Both are scope plus 7, which is what they have always been -- 345 was 338
plus 7 -- and the +7 has to move with scope or the ceiling drops below the
work it is meant to permit.
AWK-66 re-baselined them a FOURTH time, to 351 and 157. A sixth LIYO concert
-- 1992-07-17, entered by hand in the web app rather than transcribed by a
script -- brought 5 works and 1 composer into scope: 3 works created with
it, 2 that already existed and had been out of scope because no attended
Concert reached them, and `Bach, Johann Sebastian (arr. by Stokowski)`. The
harvest was re-run rather than the guard forced, which is the same choice
AWK-64's paragraph above records making. That Bach record was merged into
the clean one later the same day (AWK-79), BEFORE AWK-82's harvest below ran,
so 158 already counts one Bach and the merge moves no guard here.
AWK-82 re-baselined them a FIFTH time, to 358 and 158. The three LISFA
festival Concerts brought 7 works and 1 composer into scope, and unusually
the delta is exactly the transcription's own: all seven Works were new and
the composer is David Diamond. Nothing already in the space was dragged
into scope behind them, which is what made AWK-64's +8-for-6 and AWK-66's
+5-for-3 the surprises they were.
NEITHER THE SEVEN WORKS NOR DIAMOND GAINS ANYTHING FROM THIS PASS, and
that is worth writing down because the ticket's checklist expects the
opposite. IMSLP has no page for David Diamond -- he is the one unresolved
